description: For each throwing hand, count distinct award-winning players. Then keep the hands whose share of the total is above the average share, and summarise them.

b.request: Count distinct award-winning players in `player_award` for each `player.throws` value after joining to `player` and excluding unmatched awards, treating blank or missing hands as one group; calculate each group’s share of the total distinct-player counts, keep groups above the average share, and return one unrounded row containing the sum of their counts, their average share, and their average excess over the average share
b.sql: WITH hand_counts AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '') AS throwing_hand, COUNT(DISTINCT pa.player_id) AS player_count FROM player_award AS pa JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = pa.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '')), shares AS (SELECT player_count, 1.0 * player_count / SUM(player_count) OVER () AS share FROM hand_counts), compared AS (SELECT player_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(player_count) AS player_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;

c.request: Using `player_award` matched to `player` (dropping awards with no matching player), tally the award winners by throwing hand (`player.throws`). Treat a blank or missing hand as its own group. Work out each hand's share of the total across all hands. Keep only the hands whose share is above the average share. For those hands, give a single row with three values: the total of their tallies, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round anything. For each throwing hand, count distinct award-winning players. Then keep the hands whose share of the total is above the average share, and summarise them.
c.sql: WITH hand_counts AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '') AS throwing_hand, COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_id) AS player_count FROM player_award AS a JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = a.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '')), hand_shares AS (SELECT throwing_hand, player_count, 1.0 * player_count / SUM(player_count) OVER () AS share FROM hand_counts), compared AS (SELECT player_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM hand_shares) SELECT SUM(player_count) AS total_tallies, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess FROM compared WHERE share > average_share

a.request: Matching each `player_award` record to its player in `player` (dropping awards with no matching player), count the distinct players who won awards for each throwing hand (`player.throws`), so a player with several awards counts only once. Treat a blank or missing hand as its own group. Work out each hand's share of the total count across all hands. Keep only the hands whose share is above the average share across hands. For those hands, give a single row with three values: the total of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH hand_counts AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '') AS throwing_hand, COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_id) AS player_count FROM player_award AS a JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = a.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '')), shares AS (SELECT throwing_hand, player_count, 1.0 * player_count / SUM(player_count) OVER () AS share FROM hand_counts), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(s.player_count) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS average_share, AVG(s.share - b.average_share) AS average_excess_share FROM shares AS s CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b WHERE s.share > b.average_share;

d.request: Join `player_award` to `player`, dropping awards with no matching player. For each throwing hand (`player.throws`), count distinct award-winning players, treating a blank or missing hand as its own group. Calculate each hand’s share of the total count across all hands, and keep only hands whose share is above the average share. Return one row with three unrounded values: the sum of the retained hands’ counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their shares exceed the average share.
d.sql: WITH hand_counts AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '') AS throwing_hand, COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_id) AS player_count FROM player_award AS a JOIN player AS p ON p.player_id = a.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '')), shares AS (SELECT player_count, 1.0 * player_count / SUM(player_count) OVER () AS share, 1.0 / COUNT(*) OVER () AS average_share FROM hand_counts) SELECT SUM(player_count) AS total_players, AVG(share) AS average_retained_share, AVG(share - average_share) AS average_excess_share FROM shares WHERE share > average_share;
